findings.title: New installations bypass the GitHub installer identity check
findings.body: When no Integration row exists yet, this branch immediately advances to integration creation without checking the GitHub account that installed the app. This is a normal race because the browser redirect from GitHub can reach this pipeline before the installation webhook has created the Integration containing `metadata.sender`; `build_integration` only fetches installation details and does not establish the installing user. A user can start their own valid Sentry/OAuth pipeline and submit a newly created/known installation ID during that window, causing the installation to be linked to their Sentry organization even though their OAuth user is not the app installer. The identity check must be performed from trustworthy installation/user data before allowing this branch, or the flow must wait for/require the webhook record with a sender.

findings.title: Existing integrations without webhook sender metadata cause a server error
findings.body: The comparison indexes `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`, but `build_integration` creates GitHub integrations without a `sender` field and all integrations created before this change also lack it. If such an Integration remains after its OrganizationIntegration is removed (or was created through the no-record branch above), a later installation attempt reaches this code and raises KeyError instead of returning the intended installation failure response. Treat missing or malformed sender metadata as an unverified request and return the error page (or migrate/populate the metadata) rather than indexing it directly.
